title: Is the block of one divided by seventeen a cyclic number?
description: One is divided by seventeen to find the repeating block of sixteen digits, and the block is multiplied by two to see its digits cycle round. Keeko doubts that the block has fifteen digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: the zero at the start of the block is a digit of the block, and it counts. Watch for children who drop the zero and count only fifteen digits.

source: Find the repeating block of 1 ÷ 17 and check that it behaves like 142857.
video_script.why: The child has seen that the block one four two eight five seven cycles round when multiplied, and now tests whether the block of one divided by seventeen does the same.
video_script.substitution: the book's own division of one by seventeen and the check by two
video_script.anchor: One divided by seventeen, and the block that repeats
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip leaves out the zero at the start and calls five eight eight two three five two nine four one one seven six four seven the block. After the last seven the next digit is zero again, so the zero belongs to the block.
video_script.payoff_line: The block is another cyclic number.

final_answer.spoken: the block zero five eight eight two three five two nine four one one seven six four seven is another cyclic number

maths_rules: 142857 × 2 = 285714, the same digits cycled round; a number like this is called a cyclic number
1 ÷ 17: the remainders are 10, 15, 14, 4, 6, 9, 5, 16, 7, 2, 3, 13, 11, 8, 12, 1, which takes all 16 values from 1 to 16 before 1 returns
the block 0588235294117647 has 16 digits, and the zero counts
video_script.design: One idea: the block of one divided by seventeen has sixteen digits, with a zero at the start that counts, and its double cycles the same digits. Assumes the block one four two eight five seven. Wrong idea: dropping the zero and counting fifteen digits. The division stays all video; the block appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide one by seventeen by long division. Each remainder is smaller than seventeen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Here, the remainders take every value from one to sixteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Only then does the remainder one come back. That gives sixteen digits in the block.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, write the digits as they come out. After the point they are zero, five, eight, eight, two, three, five, two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then nine, four, one, one, seven, six, four, seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>After that last seven the remainder is one again. The digits begin again from the zero.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, multiply the block by two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two times the block starts with one, one, seven, six, four, seven, zero, five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then it goes on with eight, eight, two, three, five, two, nine, four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>These are the same sixteen digits, going round the circle from a different place.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the block has fifteen digits, because the first zero does not count.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But after the last seven the remainder is one, and ten shared by seventeen gives zero.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The zero comes again, so it belongs to the block. The block has sixteen digits.
